The lighthouse cottage that sold for a single coin

When the harbor trust put the keepers’ cottage at Gannet Rock up for sale last spring, it set one condition: the buyer had to keep the light’s old logbooks on the island and open the cottage to schoolchildren twice a year. The price, the trust said, was negotiable.

It sold on Friday for a single silver coin, minted in 1889, the year this newspaper was founded. The buyers, a retired ferry engineer and her brother, say they will spend the winter fixing the roof and the spring painting the window frames the same deep red they were when their grandfather kept the light.

AdvertisementAD300 × 250 · In-article

“We are not going to make it fancy,” said Ilse Marrow, 67, standing in the cottage’s small kitchen. “We are going to make it dry. Then we are going to put the kettle on and read every one of those logbooks, start to finish.”

The trust says the logbooks, which cover 104 years of weather, shipping and the occasional family argument, will be digitized next year. Readers with photographs of the cottage before 1960 are asked to contact the newsroom.
